# ethereum-optimism/optimism Monthly Report (June 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
June 2026 was defined by the transition to the **Lagoon** (formerly Interop) hardfork and the deprecation of `op-geth` in favor of `op-reth` for sequencing Karst+ blocks. Significant engineering effort was directed toward stabilizing the Superchain infrastructure, specifically through the integration of Flashblocks into Superchain Data Management (SDM) and the enhancement of Kona’s native single-chain proofs. Despite facing complex cyclic deadlocks in Reth’s state-trie machinery, the team successfully implemented performance-critical features like trie-state snapshotting and expanded dispute monitoring for super-permissioned games.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Interoperability & The Lagoon Hardfork
The project officially renamed the Interop hardfork to **Lagoon**, updating configurations across the OP Stack ([#21105](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21105)). 
- **Supernode Reliability:** Improved `op-supernode` stability by fixing "engine client not initialized" errors and implementing lazy dialing for the interop engine controller ([#21152](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21152)).
- **Failsafe Mechanisms:** Introduced a dedicated JSON-RPC error code (`-320602`) for interop filter failsafe rejections and added real-time metrics to monitor failsafe states ([#21205](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21205), [#21151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21151)).
- **SDM Enhancements:** Integrated Flashblocks support into Superchain Data Management and enforced block gas limits on pre-refund EVM gas ([#20738](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20738), [#21250](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21250)).

### op-reth & Kona Proofs
With `op-geth` deprecated for Karst+ sequencing ([#21188](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21188)), `op-reth` became the primary focus for protocol execution and proving.
- **Performance Optimization:** Implemented a one-time trie-state snapshot and hashed-leaf table snapshotting to accelerate backfill performance and reduce history-bitmap walks ([#20797](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20797), [#21088](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21088)).
- **Kona Enhancements:** Validated SDM `PostExec` blocks in native single-chain proofs and migrated fault-proof action tests to the Kona-native environment ([#21034](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21034), [#21193](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21193)).
- **State Management:** Seeded the slot-preimage DB during state-dump imports to prevent crashes during backfill sync ([#21108](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21108)).

### Infrastructure & Developer Experience
- **Dispute Monitoring:** Added support for simplified super-permissioned games to `op-dispute-mon` and enabled `superroot_atTimestamp` for non-interop chains in `op-node` ([#21106](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21106), [#20581](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20581)).
- **CI/CD Improvements:** Introduced `sccache` for Rust builds to significantly reduce compile times and implemented AI-assisted code reviews via a new `rust-review` recipe ([#21227](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21227), [#21118](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21118)).
- **Documentation:** Published comprehensive guides for `op-interop-filter`, L2 Contract Manager (L2CM), and Sequencer Defined Metering (SDM) ([#21109](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21109), [#21211](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21211)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
- **Codebase Cleanup:** A massive effort was completed to remove dead Go dependencies, unused Rust crates, and orphaned CLI tools, streamlining the monorepo ([#19996](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19996), [#20015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20015)).
- **Audit Remediation:** Addressed feedback from the Lumi Security Audit regarding `doc.go` and completed the audit of Kona Proof Interop logic ([#21124](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21124), [#19920](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19920)).
- **Withdrawal Proving:** Resolved issues where the withdrawal prove script failed to support super roots ([#21113](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21113)).

### New & Active Issues
- **Reth Deadlocks:** A critical cyclic deadlock in Reth’s `StateTrieOverlayManager` was identified as the cause for CL sync recovery stalls. Two candidate fixes are currently being tested upstream ([#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21076)).
- **Cross-Safe Backlog:** Investigation continues into why `op-supervisor` cannot drain backlogs faster than real-time after a stall, with current findings suggesting this may be expected behavior during sequencing window expiry ([#21117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21117)).
- **Uniswap Devnet 4:** New tracking is underway for Joint Devnet 4 testing, focusing on interop message handling and network restarts ([#21260](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21260)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month showed high levels of coordination between the Optimism core team and the Reth maintainers to resolve deep-seated engine API timeouts. Collaboration was also evident in the rapid renaming of the Interop hardfork, requiring synchronized updates across the `superchain-registry`, `op-geth`, and documentation. The transition to `op-reth` for sequencing has prompted a surge in "Chain Operator" documentation and migration guides, indicating a strong focus on supporting external ecosystem participants through this technical shift.
